sentences.translation: # Fall of the Teacher
The telephone was over at six o'clock in the afternoon.
Tachibana Risuko left a receiver and could not move for a while.
The call from the guardian lasted more than 30 minutes.
The story was about how to deal with a child in a class, but it was criticized by Risshi himself from the middle.
I have to keep an eye on it more.
Why didn't you notice?
He kept on saying that in a quiet but sharp voice.
I think so.
I thought so, so it was a pain.
I fell on the sofa without taking off my coat.
I looked at the ceiling.
White, nothing ceiling.
How many times have you looked up at this ceiling since you divorced and moved to your current apartment?
At first, I felt that every time I saw it, it was a room I didn't know.
But it’s a little different these days.
I'm a little used to this whiteness.
Even so, I'm tired tonight.
After he lay down enough, Risshi got up.
I forgot to check the mailbox.
I have to go get it before dinner.
Something may have arrived today.
When I went down the stairs to the entrance, I saw Morikawa Ayumi, who was in the second room, opening the mailbox.
"Ah, Mr. Tachibana,"
Ayumi raised her hand lightly.
She is a young woman over ten years old than Risshi, and seems to be doing freelance work.
It is often the hallway where you meet each other, and they always greet you brightly.
"Hello," said Risshi.
My voice was lower than usual.
"You're late today. Did you do your job?"
"Yes, a little,"
Risshi opened her mailbox.
A leaflet and a piece of paper that was transferred from school.
That was all.
"It's hard,"
said Ayumi suddenly.
It was not a blaming or comforting word, but just a saying that it looked like it.
Risshi did not speak for a moment.
"... is that so?"
I returned it.
Ayumi was shy and walked toward the stairs, saying, "Good workout."
The conversation ended with that.
I might not have had a minute.
A single person remained at the entrance, and Risshi stood with the mail in her chest.
It seems to be hard.
The word was smearing into my chest.
It’s been a long time since someone said “it’s been a big deal.
I felt like I shouldn't be showing up in school, and I always pretended to be calm.
And of course, in front of parents.
You must not be considered a weak teacher.
So I laughed, scolded and said, "It's OK."
I wish I had told someone earlier, but I couldn't say why.
For dinner, miso soup was made from tofu and onion in the refrigerator.
And only rice.
I had a little more proper food at my house where I lived before my divorce.
There was a reason for that, but it was a little related to the fact that the kitchen of that house was wider.
The kitchen is small now.
But that's enough for your own sake.
I'm going to think so.
After eating, I prepared for tomorrow's class.
I have to go to school tomorrow.
I have to organize and face her again.
I don’t know if I can, but I have to.
Around ten o'clock at night, Risshi looked out the window drinking tea.
In November, Osaka finally began to cool down at night.
The wind carried thin leaves through the light of the streetlight.
I'm getting used to my room.
I think that's true.
From the beginning, the moments when you feel this place are increasing.
One of the reasons may be that people like Ayumi are in the same building.
It was just one word.
* The main grammar used in this story*
** ※ ※ ('I must go' or 'I must face'): It represents obligations and needs.
It is almost the same as "I have to do it," but it is a somewhat hard impression.
- ** For the sake of ~** (the feeling behind "why is it so hard to work for children"): It represents the purpose or cause (for ~).
In this episode, Risshi is used in the context of showing the weight of the motivation to "do your best for someone".
** ** ('I should have told you, I couldn't tell you why'): It represents the opposite of the two when expectations, hopes and reality differ.
The nuances of dissatisfaction and regret about oneself and the situation are strong.
** ** ** ('I wish I had told someone sooner'): It represents regret for past actions.
It was a structure that said, 'I should have done (but I didn't).'
